newsitem.title: USA: Va. Power sees 911 MW nuke at full power Sat.
newsitem.headline: Va. Power sees 911 MW nuke at full power Sat.

text.p: Virginia Power Co said Friday it expected its 911 megawatt (MW) North Anna 1 nuclear unit to resume full output Saturday after being off line Thursday due to an electrical problem.
"Unit 1 is now on line. It will be ramped up to 30 percent for a number of hours with 100 percent status tomorrow," said a company spokesman.
North Anna 1's shutdown occurred when an electrical relay to a generator opened, tripping the generator and then the reactor.
"The problem at unit 1 seemed to be nothing more than a bad delay," he said.
Meanwhile, the company aimed to restart the 909 MW North Anna's unit 2 some time today, and to restore it to full power Sunday, the spokesman said.
"Unit 2 should be on line before noon, will go to five percent hold for chemistry check, be at 30 percent prior to midnight, and be at 100 percent Sunday," he said.
North Anna 2 was shut Monday to replace a section of a high-pressure turbine balance pipe after two leaks were discovered.
"We did find some evidence of wear (at unit 1), but not to the extent of unit 2," the spokesman said, adding the company considered the degree of corrosion in unit 1's balance pipe minor.

Virginia Power, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources, is the operator and has an 88.4 percent stake in North Anna complex in Mineral, Va., while Old Dominion Electric Co-operative holds the remaining 11.6 percent.
Virginia Power also operates two 781 MW units at its Surry nuclear facility in Gravel Neck, Va. Both Surry units were operating at 100 percent power, the spokesman said.
The four nuclear units accounted for 32 percent of Virginia Power electricity deliveries in 1995.
